# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart valve issue, which may involve monitoring and potential treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, including trouble latching on and getting upset during feeds.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue, which may affect his posture and movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with his ears, particularly with loud noises, and has had otitis media or glue ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many individuals with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where the front of his eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups to prevent tooth decay and maintain overall oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental issues can be a concern for individuals with KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and the need for frequent visits to the dentist.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from mainstream education.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental differences, including a delayed onset of certain milestones and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have developmental delays and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can result in various complications such as sacral dimple and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews at age 5, and palatal reviews if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve issues, consideration of tethered cord review and investigation based on clinical concerns, management of hip dysplasia and sensorimotor development based on individual needs.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects his vision clarity, particularly when reading or watching television.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences hypotonia, which affects his muscles' strength and balance, leading to slow progress in speech therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and affect his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss and affect their hearing.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, where his front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are prone to chipping or breaking, requiring frequent visits to the dentist.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and struggles to express himself effectively, which impacts his educational performance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome may need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream settings with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and behavioral differences, including hypotonia and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, most individuals with KBG syndrome have developmental delay, with some showing more obvious delay and others displaying more variability in their overall development.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and hip dysplasia, in which the hip joints are easily dislocated.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Subtle anomalies of the palate and tethered cord can also be present in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology check-ups.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart condition, treatment of palatal abnormalities, protection of teeth against damage, strengthening of muscles through physical therapy, and speech therapy to aid communication.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart checks to ensure everything is okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky with food and some things he just won't eat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and needs medication to manage it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences otitis media or glue ear, which can affect his hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity to cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent visits to the dentist are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed extra help in school and requires support to achieve academic goals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, which is linked to his feeding difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may have various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis, and there are concerns regarding the formation of his palate.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have anomalies of the roof of the mouth (palate), which can affect feeding and speech development.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic cardiology assessments.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Management of epilepsy with medication, monitoring of heart conditions, correction of palatal abnormalities, and consideration of additional therapies based on individual needs.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away, requiring glasses to help correct this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism (the front of the eye is not perfectly rounded, causing blurry vision) and short- or long sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and frequent cavities, requiring regular dental visits.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty expressing herself clearly, leading to frustration for both her and those around her.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: She has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away. We've gotten her glasses to help correct this, and it's made a big difference in her ability to see the board at school and read books comfortably.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Sometimes she doesn't respond right away when we call her name. It's like she's not hearing us or is too focused on what she's doing to notice. This has been a bit of a concern for us because we worry she might be missing important instructions or warnings.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods can be a challenge for her. She tends to avoid meats and tougher vegetables because they hurt her teeth or are hard to bite through. We've had to adapt meal times to include softer options or cut her food into smaller pieces to make eating easier.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, there's an issue with one of the valves in her heart. Regular check-ups with the cardiologist have become a routine part of our lives now. So far, everything has been stable, but we remain vigilant for any changes or signs that something might be off.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Occasionally, she'll have these episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't seem to be with us anymore. These blank spells can be alarming because we never know when they might happen or how long they'll last. It's been a point of discussion with her neurologist to understand and manage these episodes better.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Feeding has been a significant issue. She has a strong aversion to certain tastes and textures, which limits her diet considerably. Mealtime can sometimes feel like a battle because of this, trying to find foods she'll eat without gagging or pushing them away.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the heart valve issue and feeding difficulties, we've also noticed she struggles with speech clarity. There are moments when her words aren't clear or she seems to jumble them together. Additionally, there are palatal abnormalities we're keeping an eye on. These various challenges require close monitoring and regular visits to several specialists to ensure we're doing everything possible to support her health and development.

Parent: Actually, yes. He tends to sit very close to the TV or when reading books, which makes me worry about his eyesight. I've tried to get him to sit farther away, but it's hard to break the habit.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Actually, he often asks people to repeat themselves because he didn't catch what they said the first time. It's like he's having trouble hearing or understanding speech sometimes.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His front teeth are noticeably larger than usual. The dentist mentioned it might be related to his jaw alignment or bite, but nothing too serious at this point.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There is a structural issue with his heart that was identified during a routine check-up. So far, it hasn't caused significant problems in daily life, but we monitor it closely.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, yes. He experiences seizures occasionally. They can be scary, but thankfully they're under control with medication.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Well, feeding has been an adventure. He shows a strong aversion to certain foods and textures. Sometimes meals end in tantrums if he's presented with something new or unappealing.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Besides the heart condition and seizures, another concern is his delayed speech development. It takes longer for him to articulate thoughts and form coherent sentences compared to peers. Additionally, there's an ongoing investigation into some undescended test results that require further examination.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that requires close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and has a strong aversion to certain foods and textures, leading to tantrums during meal times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are controlled with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to sit very close to screens or books, suggesting possible ear-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and palatal abnormalities can lead to various ear-related issues in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects his vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and frequent visits to the dentist are recommended to prevent complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school and requires some assistance with tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and speech delay, taking longer to develop certain skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature, with some individuals showing significant delay and others displaying more variability.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which may contribute to an increased curvature of the spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience anomalies such as tethered cord, which can impact movement and posture.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic examinations to monitor heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A
Note: N/A indicates information is unavailable for the specified category.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: Sometimes he just stares off into space. It's really scary because he doesn't respond for a few seconds. It's happened a handful of times already.

Parent: He was born with hip dysplasia. We've had several appointments about it and are waiting for the next steps in treatment. That's all for now.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart, which requires monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding challenges, being very picky and refusing certain textures or smells.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences staring spells and lacks responsiveness for brief periods, which can be concerning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media, a buildup of fluid in the ear, which required treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has presented with various vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty with hard foods and requires regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding has always been a challenge for the patient, and he has required short-term nasogastric tube feeding.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed additional support in school, with some children requiring EHCP and others benefiting from specialist settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, as well as palatal abnormalities and undescended testes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to scoliosis and hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic reviews for heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart conditions, treatment of palatal abnormalities, consideration of hormonal treatments, and evaluation for tethered cord based on clinical findings.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when playing or running around.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing or running around, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, specifically with bottle feeding and spitting up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, characterized by low muscle tone, which has been managed with physical therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences sensitivity to cold temperatures, indicating possible ear-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can lead to conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delays and palatal abnormalities, which may impact her vision and communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity to cold foods and drinks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent visits to the dentist are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional support in school and may need accommodations to assist with learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some achieving mainstream qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits speech delays and palatal abnormalities, impacting her development and communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is a common feature, with some individuals reaching milestones around the typical age and others requiring support.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which may contribute to an increased curvature of the spine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Various skeletal anomalies can be observed in individuals with KBG syndrome, including hip dysplasia and tethered cord.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic examinations to monitor heart rate and respiratory rate during physical activity.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Addressing hypotonia through physical therapy, managing any associated palatal abnormalities, and considering interventions for specific medical concerns as they arise.

Parent: She can't seem to keep up with the other kids when they play. Even simple games like tag leave her out of breath and she gets tired easily. I fear it might be something more serious with her heart, maybe it's not pumping properly? I just want what's best for her.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient gains weight slower than expected and grows at a rate below the 2nd centile.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired fast when playing outside and can't keep up with friends, indicating possible neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and behavioral differences.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class and gets tired easily, suggesting potential ear or nose issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing the board in class and gets tired easily, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently due to various dental concerns.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences rapid breathing when running around, which may indicate respiratory issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breath rate increases faster than normal when exerting herself, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky about food and refuses to eat certain items.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are classified as epilepsy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is sensitive to loud noises, indicating possible otitis media or glue ear.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty seeing clearly, particularly when reading or watching television.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and myopia, and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires frequent dental visits and has weak enamel, requiring close monitoring and intervention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting in some individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges in school, needing extra help and potentially struggling with certain subjects or tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely, with some children obtaining qualifications and others requiring support in mainstream settings.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, as well as palatal abnormalities and scoliosis.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A proportion of individuals with KBG syndrome have subtler anomalies of the palate, which can affect speech development and feeding, and referance for specialist review may be appropriate in some cases.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
The main recommendations for screening and treatments based on the provided consultation are:

a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing reviews to age 5 (if not previously responded to).
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
d) Check position of testes in boys.
e) Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).
f) Consider a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) following diagnosis.
g) Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist (to determine bone age), hip, spine and skull) in children following diagnosis.
h) Consider review and investigation for tethered cord (MRI) where clinical concerns arise on an individual basis (especially if sacral dimple is present).
i) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
j) Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy.

These recommendations are based solely on the information provided in the consultation and clinical reference guidelines.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural heart abnormality that requires close monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty eating and digesting food properly, making mealtimes a struggle.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach milestones like walking or sitting, and is being monitored for development to ensure progress is as expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, which has caused issues with her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasal grommet insertion to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things far away and requires glasses to correct this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty eating and digesting food properly, leading to frequent toothaches and cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns are common in KBG syndrome, including weak enamel and need for frequent dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty reaching milestones and taking longer to acquire skills compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, some children with KBG syndrome may need additional support and some benefit from specialized settings, while others can thrive in mainstream settings with appropriate support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to reach milestones like walking or sitting, indicating potential developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, most people with KBG syndrome experience delays in achieving key milestones, but there is a wide range of eventual abilities, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including delayed fontanelle closure and hip dysplasia, which can impact posture and movement.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic monitoring of heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay, behavioral differences, or speech delay.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced fluid in her ear, which has caused discomfort and potentially affected her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can lead to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned blurry vision at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences discomfort when cold foods and drinks are consumed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs frequent visits to the optician due to vision problems.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient avoids cold foods and drinks due to tooth sensitivity.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental concerns such as weak enamel and frequent cavities are common in individuals with KBG syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires additional support in school, indicating potential learning difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely; some children with KBG syndrome achieve mainstream qualifications, while others may need more support.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and those with chromosome deletions may have more significant problems.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular heart check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties when she was tiny, but it's much better now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to learn how to walk and sit than other kids her age, indicating possible neurological development delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had otitis media, a buildup of fluid in the ear, which could potentially affect her hearing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means she's a bit long-sighted, requiring glasses to correct her vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs regular dental check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: For those with significant dental concerns, regular dental visits are crucial.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has needed extra help in school, with some children needing more support and others benefiting from specialized settings.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some achieving mainstream qualifications and others requiring additional support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to learn how to walk and sit than other kids her age, suggesting potential developmental delays.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay is common in individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children acquiring mobility and other skills around the same age as “typical” children and others showing more obvious delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including delayed fontanelle closure and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, periodic hearing reviews, and palatal reviews.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring heart conditions, addressing hormonal imbalances, managing neurological conditions, treating palatal abnormalities, and correcting skeletal anomalies as they arise.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties swallowing certain textures and requires specialized help with feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are managed through speech therapy to improve her communication skills.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced issues with fluid in her ear and needs regular check-ups to monitor her condition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have had issues with otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty with clarity when trying to talk, leading to speech delay and potential challenges in understanding others.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups and takes precautions to prevent tooth decay and maintain good oral health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to detect and address any issues early.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient benefits from additional support in school and may require accommodations to assist with learning and development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Education outcomes vary widely among individuals with KBG syndrome, with some children obtaining qualifications and others needing more support.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits developmental delays and has speech delay, clarity challenges, and difficulties with feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some individuals with KBG syndrome have an increased curvature of the spine, and a small number may experience hip dysplasia or tethered cord, which can impact movement and posture.

a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic review of palatal abnormalities.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring of heart valve abnormality, treatment of fluid in the ear, management of seizures, improvement of feeding difficulties through specialized help and therapy.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty swallowing some foods and textures, making mealtime challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids his age, and sometimes gets hurt pretty badly. This is concerning and needs to be addressed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear recently, which was treated with antibiotics and monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many children with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities, which may affect his vision and lead to squint (strabismus).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity and breaks or chips easily, requiring careful brushing and avoiding hard foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular visits to the dentist are essential to prevent complications.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty swallowing some foods and textures, which impacts his ability to eat and potentially affects his appetite and nutrition.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Educationally, children with KBG syndrome may need extra support and some require special schooling or have limited access to mainstream education based on their needs.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient falls more often than other kids his age and gets hurt, which is worrying and needs attention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmentally, children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with delays in reaching milestones such as mobility and speech.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which is being monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 11% of people with KBG syndrome have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, sacral dimple, and an unusual gait.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, hearing reviews, and periodic monitoring of heart conditions.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Addressing palatal abnormalities, managing scoliosis, treating seizures, ensuring proper nutrition and dental care, and providing physical therapy and occupational therapy as needed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: My son has trouble seeing the board in class, which makes learning a challenge. His teacher has noted that he often squints or leans forward to get a better view.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He's had otitis media in the past, and we've had to deal with the aftermath of that. It's been a recurring issue, but thankfully, it hasn't affected his hearing permanently.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth aren't the strongest; they break or chip easily. We've had several trips to the dentist to fix these issues, and we're trying to teach him better oral hygiene habits.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: He gets tired quickly when playing with friends or engaging in physical activities. It's like he can't keep up for long periods without needing a rest.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Unfortunately, yes. He experiences epilepsy and has to take medication regularly to manage his seizures. We work closely with his neurologist to adjust dosages and monitor his condition.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach، bowel).
Parent: Mealtime can be tough. He has sensory issues and certain textures make him uncomfortable. We're working on making mealtime more enjoyable and exploring different food options that he might like better.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Overall, my son seems behind his peers in terms of development. He also has speech delay, which we're addressing through therapy sessions. These are our main concerns outside of the issues already mentioned.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness quickly when engaging in physical activities, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and discomfort with certain textures, leading to challenges during meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Feeding difficulties and texture sensitivities are common in individuals with KBG syndrome, affecting their ability to eat comfortably and potentially impacting overall nutrition.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness quickly when playing and has epilepsy, requiring medication to manage seizures.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be managed with various medications and in some cases, surgical intervention may be necessary.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has experienced otitis media in the past and requires regular dental check-ups to prevent future issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Recurrent otitis media or glue ear can lead to conductive hearing loss, where sounds are unable to pass into the inner ear, and frequent ear infections are common in KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and palatal abnormalities, which may impact his vision and contribute to his communication challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism and short- or long sightedness, which could affect their ability to focus and interact effectively in school and social settings.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist frequently for tooth repair and prevention due to weak enamel and previous issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Dental care is crucial, and regular check-ups are essential to prevent further complications and maintain oral health.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tiredness quickly and struggles to keep up with physically demanding activities, which may limit his academic performance and participation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Students with KBG syndrome may require additional support in mainstream education, with some benefiting from specialized settings and accommodations to help them thrive.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows signs of developmental delay and lacks certain skills that "typical" children acquire around the same age, such as speech delay and palatal abnormalities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delays and behavioral differences are prevalent in KBG syndrome, with some individuals demonstrating significant challenges in areas like speech and movement compared to their peers.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of his spinal bones, which can lead to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and there are instances of hip dysplasia and tethered cord, which may influence his mobility and posture.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome may experience various skeletal anomalies, including hip dysplasia, tethered cord, and asymmetric hip creases, which can impact their overall skeletal health and mobility.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening: Regular dental check-ups, periodic hearing reviews, and ophthalmology examinations to address potential vision and eye-related issues.
b) Recommendations for treatments: Monitoring and managing cardiac conditions, addressing hormonal imbalances, managing neurological conditions through medication and therapy, treating palatal abnormalities, correcting tethered cord issues, and managing feeding difficulties through dietary adjustments and therapeutic interventions.
